questions.q: How did David cross the Linnhe Loch into Appin?
choices: He paid for two public ferries across the water
A fisherman from Henderland's flock took him in his boat
Neil Roy Macrob rowed him over in the ferry-boat
He walked the long way around the head of the loch on foot
questions.evidence: he was one of his flock

questions.q: What was the moving clump of scarlet David saw along the water-side?
choices: A herd of red deer coming down to drink
Red soldiers coming from Fort William into Appin
Women in red cloaks walking to the kirk
Tartan plaids that the tenants had hung out to dry upon the bushes
questions.evidence: it was some of the red soldiers coming from Fort William into Appin

questions.q: As David sat by the spring in the wood of Lettermore, what doubts troubled him?
choices: Whether he had enough money left to buy food
Whether he should join an outlaw like Alan at all
Whether he had taken the wrong road to Balachulish
Whether the boatman would tell the soldiers about him
questions.evidence: why I was going to join myself with an outlaw and a would-be murderer like Alan

questions.q: Which four travellers came through the wood?
choices: A red-headed gentleman, a lawyer, a servant and a sheriff's officer
Three red-coat soldiers and the captain who led them
James of the Glens with two of his sons and a piper
A minister, a schoolmaster, a drover and a beggar
questions.evidence: knew him at once to be a sheriff's officer

questions.q: What did the servant's tartan, in Campbell colours, show about his master?
choices: That his master was a poor tenant of Appin
That his master was a Campbell in favour with the Government
That his master had just come home from France
That his master was an old and trusted friend of James of the Glens
questions.evidence: I would have known the tartan to be of the Argyle (or Campbell) colours

questions.q: What question did David ask the red-headed gentleman?
choices: The way to Aucharn
The way to Balachulish
Where Alan Breck was
Where to find a ferry
questions.evidence: I rose up from the bracken and asked him the way to Aucharn

questions.q: Who turned out to be the red-headed gentleman David had stopped?
choices: Mungo, a lawyer from Edinburgh
Colin Roy Campbell of Glenure, the Red Fox
Hector Maclean, the rich man of Mull
The sheriff of Argyle, come to arrest James Stewart
questions.evidence: Colin Roy Campbell of Glenure, him they called the Red Fox

questions.q: Glenure says the lad "speers if I am on the way to Aucharn." What does "speers" mean here?
choices: Shouts
Asks
Hopes
Warns
questions.evidence: speers if I am on the way to Aucharn

questions.q: What happened just as Glenure turned to look at the lawyer?
choices: The soldiers came marching around the bend
A shot was fired from up the hill and he fell
Alan Breck stepped out from behind a tree
His horse took fright on the narrow track and threw him down
questions.evidence: there came the shot of a firelock from higher up the hill

questions.q: What did the man David saw running away up the hill look like?
choices: A big man in a black coat with metal buttons and a long gun
A small man in a tartan kilt carrying a sword
A red-headed man in a long green coat carrying a brace of pistols
A thin old man with a white wig and a staff
questions.evidence: He was a big man, in a black coat, with metal buttons, and carried a long fowling-piece

questions.q: What did the lawyer shout to the soldiers about David?
choices: That David was the one who fired the shot
Ten pounds if they took him, since he was an accomplice
That David was a brave lad who should be helped
That David must be shot on sight as a rebel and a Jacobite spy
questions.evidence: Ten pounds if ye take that lad!

questions.q: Why did the lawyer's words fill David with "quite a new kind of terror"?
choices: He was afraid the soldiers would beat him
He was now in danger of losing both his life and his good name
He realized the lawyer knew his uncle Ebenezer
He thought the murderer would come back for him
questions.evidence: it is one thing to stand the danger of your life, and quite another to run the peril of both life and character

questions.q: A voice tells David to "Jock in here among the trees." What does "jock" mean here?
choices: Run fast
Duck
Climb
Hide your face

questions.q: Why did Alan keep standing up to his full height and looking back as they ran?
choices: He wanted the soldiers to see them and follow the wrong way
He was trying to spot where the man who had shot Glenure was hiding
He was looking for a safe path back down to the loch
He was checking that David was still keeping up
questions.evidence: every time he did so, there came a great far-away cheering and crying of the soldiers

questions.q: What is the most important event in this chapter?
choices: David being robbed by a fisherman on the Linnhe Loch
The Red Fox being shot, and David being blamed as an accomplice
David finally reaching the house of James of the Glens
Alan and David being captured by the soldiers
